defect_candidates.title: Full-output spill initialized after destructive tail pruning
conditions: The execution callback delivers more than the 102400 UTF-8-byte retained-tail cap before execution settles.
Capture pruning has removed an initial prefix, progress reports truncation, and no full-output file has previously been requested.
Post-execution temporary-file creation and append succeed.
defect_candidates.result: The returned full-output path contains the retained tail only; the discarded prefix is irrecoverable from this capture. This finding does not require the separate OS pipe-draining defect to be present.

provenance.scope: Attribution read from local Git history only; no upstream remote was queried.

defect_candidates.test_gap: The inspected existing Bash spill test uses 2001 short lines, which crosses the 2000-line presentation limit but does not cross the retained-tail byte cap. It does not establish preservation beyond 100 KiB.

defect_candidates.title: Byte-bounded multi-line tail metadata recount ignores byte bound
conditions: At least two complete tail lines fit the byte bound, but fewer than min(total_lines,max_lines) lines fit.
The single-partial-last-line path is not taken.
defect_candidates.result:
The emitted tail is right, but output_lines reports min(total_lines,max_lines) rather than the number emitted. Source-derived example: aaaa
bbbb
cccc with max_bytes=9 and max_lines=2000 emits bbbb
cccc but reports three lines.
defect_candidates.consequence: Bash start-line/range notices derived from output_lines can misidentify the retained range.
defect_candidates.test_gap: Existing common truncation/partial-line cases do not prove the byte-bound multi-line recount.

provenance.scope: Current frozen source and SHA-256 verified; historical originating commit was not independently attributed for this candidate.

defect_candidates.title: Mutation admission order and missing-target alias resolution differ
conditions: Two mutation calls for the same canonical target begin in an order opposite to completion of asynchronous key resolution; or
A nonexistent target is addressed through a symlinked existing ancestor or dangling link and through its canonical spelling.
defect_candidates.result: Rust does not queue registration before resolving keys, so later invocation can acquire the lock first. When canonicalize fails for missing targets it uses lexical absolute paths, so equivalent missing-target aliases can acquire distinct locks.
defect_candidates.consequence: Current coding-agent invocation-order/alias exclusion cannot be assumed from the existing per-key mutex.
defect_candidates.test_gap: The sharing test uses equivalent literal paths instead of real symlinks and permits either final write order. Abort-bracketing tests support holding locks through I/O but do not settle admission ordering.

defect_candidates.title: Unique exact edit can conflict with a separate fuzzy lookalike
conditions: The original content has exactly one exact occurrence of oldText and an additional distinct occurrence that becomes equal after fuzzy normalization.
defect_candidates.result: Rust follows the older normalize/rescan/count algorithm; it may reject the unique exact edit as ambiguous or select a normalized location, whereas current coding-agent requires the unique exact occurrence to win and retain its original position.
defect_candidates.consequence: A valid precise edit can fail or lose the exact-location guarantee.
defect_candidates.test_gap: Rust exact/fuzzy happy paths and error atomicity tests do not cover current exact-precedence regression bodies.

defect_candidates.title: Display formatter emits replacement new block as both added and removed
conditions: The diff library supplies a Replace operation to the display diff formatter.
defect_candidates.result: The branch chooses new_lines for raw, marks both is_added and is_removed, emits that same new text with both markers, and advances old/new counters by the replacement new length.
defect_candidates.consequence: Old removed text is not represented correctly; unequal replacement lengths also corrupt subsequent display line numbering. The separate unified patch uses the library's proper builder, so display and patch can disagree.
defect_candidates.test_gap: The inspected test only checks that new text is present. This finding is conditional source reasoning, with no runtime reproduction.

defect_candidates.title: Temporary log ownership is not implemented by filesystem cleanup
conditions: Rust capture creates a temporary log and FileSystem.cleanup is subsequently called.
defect_candidates.result: create_temp_dir forgets the temporary-directory owner; create_temp_file uses such a directory. cleanup only kills/clears tracked PIDs and has no tracked temporary paths to remove.
defect_candidates.consequence: A future retained-shell implementation must add explicit per-session log cleanup/retention; the current temporary-file API does not provide TS registry cleanup.

upstream_quirks_to_avoid_copying.finding: TS direct-argv timeout escalation checks !proc.killed after SIGTERM; proc.killed means a signal was sent, not that the process exited. Pre-aborted signals are checked after spawn, and stdout/stderr capture is unbounded.
Find's cancellation callback can run during the async .git probe before stopChild is installed, after which the source can still spawn fd; no final pre-spawn abort recheck is present.

Grep has setup windows before the abort listener is attached and removes the listener on process close before later asynchronous context reads; do not infer fully cancellable setup/context processing.
Input budgets advance before writing; pending means drain/close/error did not establish success before the bound, so pending bytes must not be resent. Execution AbortSignal is unused by the tool.
